title: Managing Breakouts
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/0/body: Your stop loss belongs where, if price gets there, **the breakout has failed**. For an upside breakout, common spots are **below the broken level**, **below the breakout candle's low** or **below the last low inside the range**.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/0/visual/sy: Stop below the level and the breakout candle
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/1/body: A very tight stop lets you trade bigger for the same risk, but normal noise can knock you out **for no reason**. A structural stop is safer, but your **position gets smaller**. Always add a **buffer** of a few pips, too.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: To buy after this breakout, which line is the more sensible spot for your stop loss?
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/2/explanati: A sits below the broken level and the breakout candle's low. If price gets there, the breakout really is dead. B is inside the breakout candle's body and gets hit by a normal pullback. C is far away for no reason and shrinks your position a lot.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/3/prompt: You risk $100 per trade. How much should each pip of your position be worth?
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/3/explanati: The stop is 25 pips away, and 100 ÷ 25 = $4 per pip. On EUR/USD, where one standard lot is about $10 per pip, that's about 0.4 lots.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: A structural stop goes below the last low inside the range (before the breakout). Tap the candle that made that low.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/4/explanati: The last low before the breakout formed around 60,300. The range bottom (60,000) is older. A stop below this low means: if buyers can't even hold this higher low, the breakout is invalid.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/5/statement: If price gets close to your stop loss, it's better to move the stop further away so the trade has more room.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/5/explanati: Moving your stop further away means taking more risk than you planned. Only move a stop in your favor (to your entry, for example), never the other way.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/6/sentence: If price closes back ___ the range after the breakout, the breakout has failed. That's why the stop on a buy goes ___ the broken level.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/6/explanati: A deep return into the range means the reason for the trade is gone. A stop below the level covers exactly that scenario.
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/7/pairs/0/m: Below a key level or low
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/7/pairs/1/m: Inside or just below the breakout candle
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/7/pairs/2/m: A few extra pips for noise
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/prompt: After you bought the breakout, a strong candle pushed price back into the range and closed below the level, but your stop hasn't been hit yet. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/options/0: The trade idea is invalid; many traders exit early
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/options/1: Move the stop lower to give it room
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/options/2: Double the position to improve the average
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/options/3: Remove the stop so it doesn't close for nothing
lessons/breakout-u3-l1/steps/8/explanati: A strong close inside the range means the breakout scenario is broken. Exiting early, or at least sticking to your stop, makes sense. The other options only make your risk bigger.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/0/body: A classic way to set a target: measure the **range height**, then project the same distance from the **broken level** in the breakout's direction. A range from 1.0800 to 1.0850 is 50 pips, so an upside breakout targets about **1.0900**.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/1/body: For a **triangle**, you add the height of the pattern's widest part to the breakout point. For a **flag**, you add the length of the **flagpole**. These targets are **rough estimates**, not certainties, so many traders take some profit early.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/1/tip: If there's a major resistance before the target, make that resistance your first target.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: EUR/USD ranged between 1.0820 and 1.0860, and price broke out above the top. Where's the measured target?
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/2/explanati: The range is 40 pips tall (1.0860 − 1.0820). Go 40 pips above the broken level: 1.0860 + 0.0040 = 1.0900.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: Bitcoin ranged between $58,000 and $62,000, and the range bottom broke to the downside. Where's the measured target?
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/3/explanati: The range is $4,000 tall. It's a downside breakout, so subtract from the range bottom: 58,000 − 4,000 = 54,000. 66,000 would be the target for an upside breakout.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/4/prompt: GBP/USD broke out of its range to the upside. Mark the measured move target with a line.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/4/explanati: Range height = 1.2700 − 1.2640 = 60 pips. Add that distance above the breakout point (the range top): 1.2700 + 0.0060 = 1.2760. It's an estimated target, not a guaranteed one.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: Gold broke the top of this range. Where's the measured target?
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/5/explanati: The range is $20 tall (2400 − 2380). $20 above the broken level gives you 2420.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/6/statement: A measured target guarantees price will reach that exact level.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/6/explanati: This method is just a statistical estimate. Price may turn early or run much further, which is why many traders take some profit before the target.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps for setting a range breakout target in order.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/7/items/0: Mark the range top and bottom
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/7/items/2: Add the height to the broken level
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/7/items/3: Take some profit near the target
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/7/explanati: No top and bottom, no height. Once the target is worked out, you manage profits as price gets near it.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/8/sentence: In a bull flag, you add the length of the ___ above the breakout point.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/8/explanati: The flagpole is the sharp move before the pause. The usual assumption is that after the breakout, a move of about the same size repeats.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/9/prompt: The 58,000 to 59,000 range broke to the upside, and the target is 60,000. Tap the first candle that reached the target.
lessons/breakout-u3-l2/steps/9/explanati: The range is $1,000 tall, so the target is 60,000. This is the first candle whose high reached 60,000, and its upper wick shows some traders took profit right there.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/0/body: When price pops above resistance but **falls back into the range**, breakout buyers get **trapped**, and their stop losses (which are sell orders) can **speed up** the drop. That's why many traders see a fakeout as a chance to trade in the **opposite direction**.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/0/tip: It's the same idea as a liquidity sweep in Smart Money Concepts, just under another name.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/1/body: **Entry:** after a candle closes **back inside the range**. **Stop loss:** just above the **fake high**. **Target:** the middle of the range or the **other side of the range**. If price closes above the fake high again, the setup is invalid.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: Bitcoin closed above 61,000, but the next candle fell back into the range on high volume. Which move is more likely?
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/2/explanati: The breakout didn't hold, and a high-volume bearish candle pushed price back into the range. Trapped buyers may add fuel to the drop as they sell. A move toward the range bottom is more likely, with a stop loss above the fake high.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: Which candle confirmed the fakeout? (The first candle that closed back inside the range after the breakout.)
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/3/explanati: The previous candle closed above 2400 on low volume, and this one closed back below 2400 on high volume. That close inside the range is the trigger for a fakeout sell.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/4/prompt: Where does the stop loss go on a sell after a fakeout above the range top?
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/4/options/0: Just above the fake wick's high
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/4/options/3: No need, the fakeout is certain
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/4/explanati: If price climbs above the fake high again, the breakout was real and the sell idea is invalid. The resistance line is too close and gets hit by a simple retest.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/5/statement: Every return into the range is a sure fakeout, and price will definitely reach the range bottom.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/5/explanati: Sometimes price dips back briefly, then rallies again and completes a real breakout. A fakeout is just a probability setup, and you still need a stop loss.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: Put the steps of trading a fakeout above the range top in order.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/6/items/1: A candle closes back inside the range
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/6/items/2: Sell with a stop above the fake high
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/6/items/3: Target: the middle or bottom of the range
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/6/explanati: First the breakout has to happen, then fail (a close back inside the range). You only enter after that confirmation, and the target is the other side of the range.
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/7/prompt: What's the risk-reward on this fakeout sell?
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: The range is 1.0800 to 1.0850. Price wicked up to 1.0865 on low volume and closed at 1.0842. Which plan makes more sense?
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/options/0: Sell with a stop above 1.0865 and a target near 1.0800
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/options/1: Buy, because price went above resistance
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/options/2: Buy with a 1.0900 target from the measured move
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/options/3: Sell with no stop, since the fakeout is obvious
lessons/breakout-u3-l3/steps/8/explanati: A low-volume close inside the range means the breakout wasn't confirmed, and a measured target only makes sense for a real breakout. The fakeout setup: sell, stop above the wick, target the range bottom.
